Natural_Language: This part prescribes acquisition policies and procedures for sustainable acquisition, ensuring proper handling and notification of hazardous materials, and preventing pollution.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_000_a: Part prescribes acquisition policies and procedures for sustainable acquisition; P_23_000_b: Part prescribes policies for ensuring proper handling and notification of hazardous materials; P_23_000_c: Part prescribes policies for preventing pollution
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement. Three conjunctive purposes are independently identifiable and collectively define the part's coverage.

Natural_Language: This subpart provides policies and procedures for procuring sustainable products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_100: Subpart provides policies and procedures for procuring sustainable products
Validation_Notes: Atomic scope statement. Single self-contained declarative purpose.

Natural_Language: Definitions as used in this subpart.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101: Definitions for subpart 23.1 consist of energy-efficient product, EPA-designated item, low standby power device, ozone-depleting substance, sustainable product, and USDA-designated product category
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for all definitions in subpart. All six defined terms collectively constitute the definitional framework.

Natural_Language: Energy-efficient product means a product that meets DOE and EPA criteria for use of the ENERGY STAR trademark label; or is in the upper 25 percent of efficiency for all similar products as designated by DOE FEMP.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_1_a: Product meets DOE and EPA criteria for use of ENERGY STAR trademark label; P_23_101_1_b: Product is in the upper 25 percent of efficiency for all similar products as designated by DOE FEMP
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition: either criterion independently satisfies the definition. The 'or' is explicit in the source text.

Natural_Language: Meets Department of Energy (DOE) and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) criteria for use of the ENERGY STAR trademark label.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_1_1_a: Product meets DOE criteria for ENERGY STAR; P_23_101_1_1_b: Product meets EPA criteria for ENERGY STAR
Validation_Notes: Both DOE and EPA criteria must be met. The conjunction is implicit in 'DOE and EPA criteria.'

Natural_Language: Is in the upper 25 percent of efficiency for all similar products as designated by the DOE Federal Energy Management Program (FEMP).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_1_2: Product is in the upper 25 percent of efficiency for all similar products as designated by DOE FEMP
Validation_Notes: Atomic proposition. Single criterion with no logical sub-components.

Natural_Language: EPA-designated item means a product that is listed by EPA in a procurement guideline because it can be made with recovered material and for which EPA has provided recommended recovered material content levels.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_2_a: Product is listed by EPA in a procurement guideline because it can be made with recovered material; P_23_101_2_b: EPA has provided recommended recovered material content levels for the product
Validation_Notes: Both conditions must hold: EPA listing AND EPA-provided content levels. The 'and' is explicit.

Natural_Language: Low standby power device means a product that uses an external standby power device or contains an internal standby power function; and uses no more than one watt of electricity in its standby power consuming mode or meets recommended low standby levels as designated by DOE FEMP.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_3_a: Product uses external standby power device or contains internal standby power function; P_23_101_3_b: Product uses no more than one watt in standby mode or meets DOE FEMP low standby levels
Validation_Notes: Parent for two conjunctive criteria. Both sub-criteria (3)(1) and (3)(2) must be satisfied simultaneously.

Natural_Language: Uses an external standby power device or contains an internal standby power function.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_3_1_a: Product uses an external standby power device; P_23_101_3_1_b: Product contains an internal standby power function
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: either external device or internal function satisfies this criterion.

Natural_Language: Uses no more than one watt of electricity in its standby power consuming mode or meets recommended low standby levels as designated by DOE FEMP.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_3_2_a: Product uses no more than one watt in standby mode; P_23_101_3_2_b: Product meets recommended low standby levels as designated by DOE FEMP
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: either the one-watt threshold or DOE FEMP levels satisfy this criterion.

Natural_Language: Ozone-depleting substance means any substance the EPA designates in 40 CFR part 82 as Class I or Class II.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_4_a: Substance is designated by EPA in 40 CFR part 82 as Class I; P_23_101_4_b: Substance is designated by EPA in 40 CFR part 82 as Class II
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition: either class designation makes a substance ozone-depleting.

Natural_Language: Class I, including, but not limited to, chlorofluorocarbons, halons, carbon tetrachloride, and methyl chloroform.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_4_1: Substance is EPA-designated Class I under 40 CFR part 82, including but not limited to chlorofluorocarbons, halons, carbon tetrachloride, and methyl chloroform
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Non-exhaustive list indicates Class I scope is broader than enumerated substances.

Natural_Language: Class II, including, but not limited to, hydrochlorofluorocarbons.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_4_2: Substance is EPA-designated Class II under 40 CFR part 82, including but not limited to hydrochlorofluorocarbons
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Non-exhaustive list for Class II substances.

Natural_Language: Sustainable product means a product meeting one of four categories: recovered material, energy-efficient/low standby, biobased, or safe alternative to ozone-depleting substance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_5: Sustainable product satisfies at least one of four qualifying categories
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive parent: any one of four categories independently qualifies a product as sustainable. The numbered list without conjunctive language implies 'or.'

Natural_Language: A product that contains recovered material designated by the EPA under the Comprehensive Procurement Guidelines (42 U.S.C. 6962) (40 CFR part 247).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_5_1: Product contains recovered material designated by EPA under CPG per 42 USC 6962 and 40 CFR part 247
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Single qualifying criterion with statutory and regulatory citations.

Natural_Language: An energy-efficient product or low standby power device (42 U.S.C. 8259b) (10 CFR part 436, subpart C).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_5_2_a: Product is an energy-efficient product; P_23_101_5_2_b: Product is a low standby power device
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: either energy-efficient or low standby power qualifies. Both terms defined earlier in 23.101.

Natural_Language: A biobased product that meets the content requirements of the USDA under the BioPreferred program (7 U.S.C. 8102) (7 CFR Part 4270).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_5_3: Product is biobased and meets USDA BioPreferred content requirements per 7 USC 8102 and 7 CFR Part 4270
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Single qualifying criterion with statutory and regulatory citations.

Natural_Language: A substance identified in the EPA's Significant New Alternatives Policy (SNAP) program as a safe alternative to an ozone-depleting substance (42 U.S.C. 7671l) (40 CFR part 82, subpart G).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_5_4: Substance is identified in EPA SNAP program as safe alternative to ozone-depleting substance per 42 USC 7671l and 40 CFR part 82 subpart G
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Single qualifying criterion with statutory and regulatory citations.

Natural_Language: USDA-designated product category means a generic grouping of biobased products that are listed by USDA in a procurement guideline and for which USDA has provided minimum biobased content standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_101_6_a: Product category is a generic grouping of biobased products listed by USDA in a procurement guideline; P_23_101_6_b: USDA has provided minimum biobased content standards for the category
Validation_Notes: Both conditions must hold: USDA listing AND USDA-provided content standards.

Natural_Language: Policy for procuring sustainable products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_102: Policy consists of mandatory procurement requirement and price reasonableness consideration
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both subsections (a) and (b) collectively constitute the policy.

Natural_Language: Agencies must procure sustainable products to the maximum extent practicable. Procuring a sustainable product is considered practicable, unless the agency cannot acquire the sustainable product competitively within a reasonable performance schedule; that meets reasonable performance requirements; or at a reasonable price.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_102_a_1: Agency must procure sustainable products to maximum extent practicable; P_23_102_a_2: Procurement is practicable unless one of three exceptions applies; P_23_102_a_3: Exception - cannot acquire competitively within reasonable schedule; P_23_102_a_4: Exception - does not meet reasonable performance requirements; P_23_102_a_5: Exception - not at reasonable price
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex structure: mandatory procurement duty combined with 'unless' exceptions. The 'unless' creates a conditional where absence of all three exceptions triggers the practicability presumption. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15 for the conditional. The disjunctive exceptions mean any single exception defeats the practicability presumption.

Natural_Language: Cannot acquire the sustainable product competitively within a reasonable performance schedule.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_102_a_1: Agency cannot acquire sustainable product competitively within reasonable performance schedule
Validation_Notes: Atomic exception criterion. Stands alone as one of three disjunctive grounds for impracticability.

Natural_Language: Does not meet reasonable performance requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_102_a_2: Sustainable product does not meet reasonable performance requirements
Validation_Notes: Atomic exception criterion.

Natural_Language: Not at a reasonable price.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_102_a_3: Sustainable product is not available at a reasonable price
Validation_Notes: Atomic exception criterion.

Natural_Language: When considering whether the price of a sustainable product is reasonable, agencies should consider whether the product is cost-effective over the life of the product.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_102_b_a: Agency is considering whether price of sustainable product is reasonable; P_23_102_b_b: Agency considers whether product is cost-effective over the life of the product
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' indicates recommended but not mandatory practice. Conditional structure: when price reasonableness is being evaluated, life-cycle cost-effectiveness should be considered. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15. Non-binding guidance reduces confidence.

Natural_Language: Procedures for sustainable products procurement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_103: Procedures consist of identification, justification, and solicitation/contract requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All three procedural steps are required.

Natural_Language: Work with the requiring activity to identify sustainable products that apply to the acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_103_a: Contracting officer works with requiring activity to identify applicable sustainable products
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory procedural requirement. Imperative 'work with' functions as 'shall' in regulatory context.

Natural_Language: When it is not practicable to procure a sustainable product (see 23.102(a)), include a justification explaining the circumstances in the contract file.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_103_b_a: It is not practicable to procure a sustainable product per 23.102(a); P_23_103_b_b: Justification explaining circumstances is included in contract file
Validation_Notes: Conditional: impracticability triggers justification requirement. Cross-references 23.102(a) for the definition of impracticable. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15. The 'when' creates a clear conditional trigger.

Natural_Language: Ensure the solicitation and contract identify sustainable products that are required to be provided during performance of the contract and those that are covered by a justification described in paragraph (b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_103_c_a: Solicitation and contract identify sustainable products required during performance; P_23_103_c_b: Solicitation and contract identify products covered by justification per 23.103(b)
Validation_Notes: Both identification requirements are mandatory. Solicitation/contract must address both required and justified-exception products.

Natural_Language: Priorities for sustainable products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_104: Priorities consist of EPA-designated item preference and designated country eligibility
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both priority rules apply.

Natural_Language: When both an EPA-designated item containing recovered material and a biobased product in a USDA-designated product category could be used for the same purposes, procure the EPA-designated item.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_104_a_1: Both an EPA-designated item and a biobased product in a USDA-designated category could be used for the same purposes; P_23_104_a_2: Agency procures the EPA-designated item
Validation_Notes: Conditional priority rule: when both product types are available for same purpose, EPA-designated item takes precedence. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15. Clear mandatory preference hierarchy.

Natural_Language: Treat products from designated countries, as defined in part 25, as eligible for the preference for biobased products provided that those products meet specified conditions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_104_b: Products from designated countries per Part 25 are eligible for biobased preference if conditions met
Validation_Notes: Conditional with conjunctive antecedent: both conditions in (b)(1) and (b)(2) must be met for designated country products to qualify. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Meet the criteria for the definition of biobased product, except that the products need not meet the requirement that renewable agricultural materials or forestry materials in such product must be domestic.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_104_b_1_a: Product meets biobased product definition criteria; P_23_104_b_1_b: Product is not required to meet domestic material requirement
Validation_Notes: Conjunction of positive criterion (meets biobased definition) and negated requirement (domestic material waived). The 'except that' creates a carve-out from the standard definition.

Natural_Language: Otherwise meet all requirements for participation in the preference program.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_104_b_2: Product meets all other requirements for participation in biobased preference program
Validation_Notes: Atomic catch-all requirement. All remaining program requirements must be satisfied.

Natural_Language: Exceptions to sustainable products requirement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_105: Exceptions consist of five categories covering outside-US contracts, weapon systems, combat energy products, military biobased products, and Class II alternatives
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All five exception categories collectively define the scope of exceptions. Each is independent but together constitute the complete exception framework.

Natural_Language: Contracts performed or supplies delivered outside of the United States are not required to include sustainable products, unless the agency head determines that such application is in the interest of the United States.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_105_a_1: Contract is performed or supplies delivered outside the United States; P_23_105_a_2: Sustainable products are not required; P_23_105_a_3: Agency head determines application is in the interest of the United States
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional with 'unless' override: outside-US contracts are exempt unless agency head intervenes. The 'unless' negates the exception when agency head makes affirmative determination. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Contracts for weapon systems are not required to include sustainable products; however, compliance with applicable agency programs is required for recovered materials (see 23.107(a)(1)) (42 U.S.C. 6962) and for alternatives for ozone depleting substances (42 U.S.C. 7671l), unless a written justification exists.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_105_b_1: Contract is for weapon systems; P_23_105_b_2: Sustainable products are not required; P_23_105_b_3: Compliance with recovered materials agency programs per 23.107(a)(1) is required; P_23_105_b_4: Compliance with ozone-depleting substance alternatives is required; P_23_105_b_5: Written justification exists
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex nested conditional: weapon systems get general exemption but still must comply with recovered materials and ozone programs unless written justification. Multiple layers of conditionality. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15 twice. The 'however' creates a partial override of the exemption.

Natural_Language: Energy-consuming products or systems designed or procured for combat or combat-related missions are not required to be energy-efficient products (42 U.S.C. 8259b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_105_c_1: Product or system is energy-consuming and designed or procured for combat or combat-related missions; P_23_105_c_2: Product is not required to be energy-efficient
Validation_Notes: Conditional exemption: combat/combat-related purpose triggers energy-efficiency waiver. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15. Straightforward conditional.

Natural_Language: Biobased products to be used in military equipment (products or systems designed or procured for combat or combat-related missions), spacecraft systems, or launch support equipment are not required to meet the content requirements of the USDA under the BioPreferred program (7 U.S.C. 8102).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_105_d_1: Product is biobased and to be used in military equipment, spacecraft systems, or launch support equipment; P_23_105_d_2: Product is not required to meet USDA BioPreferred content requirements
Validation_Notes: Conditional exemption: military/spacecraft/launch use triggers BioPreferred content waiver. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15. Broader scope than 23.105(c) by including spacecraft and launch equipment.

Natural_Language: Substitution is not required for class II substances identified as safe alternatives under 42 U.S.C. 7671k, or for products made with or containing such substances, and such substances may be used as substitutes for other class I or class II substances.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_105_e_1: Class II substance is identified as safe alternative under 42 USC 7671k; P_23_105_e_2: Substitution is not required for such substance or products containing it; P_23_105_e_3: Such substances may be used as substitutes for other Class I or Class II substances
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Conditional with mixed mandatory and permissive elements. No-substitution is mandatory (not required). The 'may be used' creates permissive authority represented as tautology. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Restrictions on purchasing.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_106: Restrictions consist of three prohibitions on Class II substances, prohibited-sale products, and nonessential products
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All three restrictions apply simultaneously.

Natural_Language: Do not purchase class II substances, or products containing class II substances, for the purpose of any use prohibited under 42 U.S.C. 7671d(c) (40 CFR 82.84(a)(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_106_a_1: Product is a class II substance or contains class II substances; P_23_106_a_2: Intended use is prohibited under 42 USC 7671d(c); P_23_106_a_3: Purchase is prohibited
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition: Class II substance + prohibited use triggers purchase ban. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15. The prohibition is absolute when both conditions hold.

Natural_Language: Do not purchase products whose sale is prohibited under 42 U.S.C. 7671h, except when the products will be used by persons certified to service vehicles (40 CFR 82.84(a)(4)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_106_b_1: Product sale is prohibited under 42 USC 7671h; P_23_106_b_2: Product will be used by persons certified to service vehicles; P_23_106_b_3: Purchase is prohibited
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition with exception: sale-prohibited products cannot be purchased unless intended for certified vehicle service personnel. The 'except when' creates a carve-out. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Do not purchase nonessential products as defined under 42 U.S.C. 7671i (40 CFR 82.84(a)(4)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_106_c_1: Product is nonessential as defined under 42 USC 7671i; P_23_106_c_2: Purchase is prohibited
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition: nonessential classification triggers absolute purchase ban. No exceptions. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Agency programs for sustainable products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_107: Agency programs consist of mandatory implementation programs and specification guidance
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both mandatory programs and specification guidance apply.

Natural_Language: Each agency must implement the following programs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_107_a: Each agency must implement both recovered material and biobased product procurement programs
Validation_Notes: Parent with mandatory 'must.' Both programs are required for each agency.

Natural_Language: A program to promote the procurement of EPA-designated items that contain recovered material. This program applies to an item if the agency procures $10,000 or more worth of the item in a fiscal year. The program must meet the minimum requirements at 40 CFR 247.6.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_107_a_1_a: Agency implements program to promote procurement of EPA-designated items with recovered material; P_23_107_a_1_b: Program applies if agency procures $10,000 or more of the item per fiscal year; P_23_107_a_1_c: Program meets minimum requirements at 40 CFR 247.6
Validation_Notes: Mandatory program with threshold trigger and minimum standards. The $10K threshold activates applicability. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15 for the threshold conditional.

Natural_Language: A program to promote the procurement of biobased products in the USDA BioPreferred Program. This program applies to a product if the agency procures $10,000 or more worth of the product in a fiscal year. The program must meet the minimum requirements at 7 CFR 4270.5(b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_107_a_2_a: Agency implements program to promote procurement of biobased products in USDA BioPreferred Program; P_23_107_a_2_b: Program applies if agency procures $10,000 or more of the product per fiscal year; P_23_107_a_2_c: Program meets minimum requirements at 7 CFR 4270.5(b)
Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to 23.107(a)(1). Same $10K threshold logic for biobased products. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Agencies may use their own specifications or commercial product descriptions; however, the solicitation and contract should specify content standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_107_b_a: Agencies use their own specifications or commercial product descriptions; P_23_107_b_b: Solicitation and contract specify content standards per (b)(1) and (b)(2)
Validation_Notes: Mixed permissive and advisory. 'May' for specification choice creates tautology (discretion). 'Should' for content specification is advisory. Both sub-requirements apply regardless of specification choice.

Natural_Language: EPA-designated items be composed of the highest percentage of recovered materials practicable or meet the EPA's minimum recovered material content standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_107_b_1_a: EPA-designated items composed of highest percentage of recovered materials practicable; P_23_107_b_1_b: EPA-designated items meet EPA minimum recovered material content standards
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive advisory requirement (parent uses 'should'). Either highest practicable percentage or EPA minimum satisfies. Advisory nature inherited from parent proposition.

Natural_Language: Biobased products in the BioPreferred Program be composed of the highest percentage of biobased material practicable or meet the USDA's minimum biobased content standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_107_b_2_a: Biobased products composed of highest percentage of biobased material practicable; P_23_107_b_2_b: Biobased products meet USDA minimum biobased content standards
Validation_Notes: Parallel to (b)(1) for biobased products. Disjunctive advisory requirement. Advisory nature inherited from parent.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provisions and contract clauses for sustainable products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108: Clause requirements consist of general sustainable products, recovered material, biobased, and ozone-depleting substance clauses
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All four clause categories apply to applicable solicitations/contracts.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.223-23, Sustainable Products, in solicitations and contracts unless a written justification or exception (see 23.103(b) and 23.105, respectively) covers the entire acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_a_1: Insert clause 52.223-23 in solicitations and contracts; P_23_108_a_2: Written justification per 23.103(b) covers entire acquisition; P_23_108_a_3: Exception per 23.105 covers entire acquisition
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Default-mandatory with 'unless' exceptions. Clause insertion is required unless entire acquisition is covered by justification or exception. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15. The 'unless' creates negated antecedent.

Natural_Language: Products containing recovered material clause requirements (except COTS items).
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_b: Recovered material provisions apply except for COTS items, consisting of certification and estimate clauses
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Parent with COTS exception. When acquisition is not COTS, both sub-clause requirements apply. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Insert the provision at 52.223-4, Recovered Material Certification, in solicitations that require the delivery or specify the use of EPA-designated items.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_b_1_a: Solicitation requires delivery or specifies use of EPA-designated items; P_23_108_b_1_b: Insert provision 52.223-4 in solicitation
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion: EPA-designated item requirement triggers 52.223-4 provision. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.223-9, Estimate of Percentage of Recovered Material Content for EPA-designated Items, in solicitations and contracts exceeding $200,000 that are for, or specify the use of, EPA-designated items containing recovered materials. If technical personnel advise that estimates can be verified, use the clause with its Alternate I.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_b_2_a: Solicitation/contract exceeds $200,000; P_23_108_b_2_b: Solicitation/contract is for or specifies use of EPA-designated items with recovered materials; P_23_108_b_2_c: Insert clause 52.223-9; P_23_108_b_2_d: Technical personnel advise estimates can be verified; P_23_108_b_2_e: Use clause with Alternate I
Validation_Notes: Nested conditional: threshold + item type triggers clause insertion, with secondary conditional for Alternate I based on technical advice. Two uses of HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Biobased products solicitation provisions and contract clauses.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_c: Biobased clause requirements consist of certification provision and reporting clause
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for biobased product clauses.

Natural_Language: Insert the provision at 52.223-1, Biobased Product Certification, in solicitations, other than for acquisitions described at 23.105(d), that require the delivery or specify the use of biobased products in USDA-designated product categories; or include the clause at 52.223-2.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_c_1_a: Acquisition is not described at 23.105(d); P_23_108_c_1_b: Solicitation requires delivery or specifies use of biobased products in USDA categories; P_23_108_c_1_c: Solicitation includes clause 52.223-2; P_23_108_c_1_d: Insert provision 52.223-1
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conditional with exclusion and disjunctive triggers. Not-23.105(d) AND (biobased requirement OR 52.223-2 inclusion) triggers 52.223-1 insertion. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Require the delivery or specify the use of biobased products in USDA-designated product categories.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_c_1_i: Solicitation requires delivery or specifies use of biobased products in USDA-designated categories
Validation_Notes: Atomic trigger condition for parent 23.108(c)(1).

Natural_Language: Include the clause at 52.223-2.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_c_1_ii: Solicitation includes clause 52.223-2
Validation_Notes: Atomic trigger condition for parent 23.108(c)(1).

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.223-2, Reporting of Biobased Products Under Service and Construction Contracts, in service and construction solicitations and contracts, unless the contract will not involve the use of biobased products in USDA-designated product categories.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_c_2_a: Contract is for service or construction; P_23_108_c_2_b: Contract involves use of biobased products in USDA-designated categories; P_23_108_c_2_c: Insert clause 52.223-2
Validation_Notes: Conditional with 'unless' converted to positive conjunction. Service/construction + biobased involvement triggers clause insertion. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Products containing ozone-depleting substances clause requirements. Except for contracts for supplies delivered outside the US and its outlying areas, or services performed outside the US.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_d_a: Contract is not for supplies delivered outside US/outlying areas; P_23_108_d_b: Contract is not for services performed outside US/outlying areas; P_23_108_d: ODS clauses apply when contract is within US scope
Validation_Notes: Parent with geographic exclusion. Both sub-clauses required when within US/outlying areas scope. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: 52.223-11, Ozone-Depleting Substances, in solicitations and contracts that may include products that may contain or be manufactured with ozone-depleting substances.
Atomic_Propositions: P_23_108_d_1_a: Solicitation/contract may include products containing or manufactured with ozone-depleting substances; P_23_108_d_1_b: Insert clause 52.223-11
